answer: We formulate a secure protocol where zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions, acting as a cryptographic lantern, bind identities to dynamic opportunity-cost bonds. By tying this staking collateral to a simulated resource matrix of ferrous and shale mining indices, we construct a subgame-perfect slashing scheme. Because the penalty scaling exceeds any collusive yield, the expected utility of Sybil multiplication remains strictly negative, forcing convergence to a unique, robust Nash equilibrium.
